memory_update.text: VRT should remain the primary pure-play candidate for integrated data-center power plus thermal infrastructure; evidence is strong but valuation/pricing checks belong in a later layer.
ETN maps more to power-distribution bottlenecks than liquid cooling; track UPS, busway, PDU, switchgear, and grid-to-chip architecture evidence.
TT became more relevant after the 2026 LiquidStack acquisition; track whether direct-to-chip and immersion cooling become material versus legacy chiller exposure.
NVT is a less obvious but high-fit rack/row supplier due to CDUs, manifolds, controls, and high-density power portfolios linked to AI/HPC and OCP-style standardization.

Other plausible US-listed or US-traded names not included due to the five-candidate limit: MOD, JCI, DELL, HPE, GEV, PWR, AMZN, MSFT, GOOGL, META, and Schneider/Legrand ADRs. MOD and JCI are especially relevant for a follow-up cooling-only pass.

node: Data-center thermal management and on-site power distribution stack
summary: Expanded universe focuses on US-listed companies with direct product or platform exposure to AI data-center thermal management and on-site power distribution. The highest-fit candidates are integrated power/cooling vendors, high-density electrical distribution suppliers, full thermal-chain HVAC/liquid-cooling providers, and rack-scale AI infrastructure integrators. This is a research universe only, not a buy/sell list.
